findings.title: Visible superiority does not guarantee duration
findings.claim: The focus can grant the earlier cohorts a real advantage in furnishings and outward appearance while denying that this visible superiority proves permanence or continuing victory.
findings.mechanism: In 19:74, أَثَاثًا names household goods, وَرِءْيًا names outward appearance, قَرْنٍ names a cohort, and أَهْلَكْنَا states that the cohort was destroyed. The same furnishings word appears in 16:80 among provisions described as lasting only until a time; 21:44 places prolonged enjoyment beside the earth's diminishing and the question of victory; 19:98 repeats the destroyed-cohort formula and asks whether even one person or a whisper remains. These independent wider scenes meet the focus words and turn the comparison from a contest in visible goods into a warning that genuine worldly advantage still does not establish durable success.
findings.reader_payoff: The comparison does not need to deny that the earlier peoples looked better equipped or more impressive. Its force comes from allowing that advantage to be real and then showing that it could not secure an enduring outcome.
findings.containment: The wider parallels do not identify particular destroyed peoples or claim that every use of أثاث denotes temporary provision. The target passages provide Arabic but no target morphology; their role here is contextual resonance, not proof that 19:74 quotes them.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run publication is trusted and names exact focus anchors and branches. The cited connection rows supply exact target Arabic but no target morphology, so the wider contact is kept at the level of the supplied wording.

branch_activations.boundary: This is a contextual resonance from 16:80, not a claim that the two passages describe the same household or that the focus word itself means temporary.

findings.title: Worldly measures do not establish divine standing
findings.claim: The focus's better-than comparison is explicitly measured by furnishings and appearance; wider passages distinguish such abundance from divine honor and immunity from punishment.
findings.mechanism: The focus adjective أَحْسَنُ makes a comparative evaluation, then the following nouns bound it to material goods and outward appearance. In 89:15 a person treats generous provision as proof that his Lord honored him; in 34:35 speakers claim that greater wealth and children mean they will not be punished, and 34:36 answers that God expands or restricts provision as He wills. These external claims meet the focus's evaluative word and its concrete goods: they change the scope of better from a worldly comparison into a question the passage does not settle about honor or safety.
findings.reader_payoff: A reader can keep the factual comparison intact without mistaking greater possessions or a better appearance for a verdict about worth or protection.
findings.containment: These are wider parallels, not a claim that 19:74 quotes 89:15 or 34:35-36, or that its earlier cohorts made the same speeches. The connection rows supply target Arabic without target morphology, so the shared inference is stated at the level of content.

epistemic.reason: The supplied connection rows include exact target Arabic but no target morphology or lexical analysis. The finding is limited to their explicit claims about provision, honor, wealth, and punishment.

branch_activations.carrier: أَحْسَنُ is the focus's positive comparative evaluation, bounded by the two worldly measures that follow it.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: In 89:15 a person receives generous provision and says that his Lord has honored him, exposing the inference from material benefit to divine regard.
branch_activations.activation: The wider claim about honor meets the focus's word for being better, while the focus itself restricts that comparison to furnishings and outward appearance.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus can acknowledge visible excellence without turning it into a judgment of divine honor.
branch_activations.boundary: The parallel does not identify the speakers in 89:15 with the earlier cohorts or claim that the focus directly quotes that passage.
